source.organization: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)

general_guidance.text: Diabetes nutrition education includes planning balanced meals and drinks while considering food choices, amounts, and timing.
general_guidance.source_section: How can I plan what to eat or drink when I have diabetes?

general_guidance.text: Meal timing can depend on medicines, physical activity, and other health conditions, so individualized planning belongs with a health care team.
general_guidance.source_section: Find the best times to eat or drink

foods_emphasized.text: Examples in healthy meal patterns include nonstarchy vegetables, fruit, whole grains, protein foods, and dairy or plant-based dairy products.
Water and other drinks with little or no added sugar are included among the source's beverage examples.

foods_limited.text: The source identifies foods high in saturated fat or sodium, sugary foods, and sweetened drinks as items to limit.

relevant_nutrients.text: Carbohydrates can raise blood glucose and are one consideration in meal planning.
The source highlights fiber, healthy fats, vitamins, and calcium in food choices.

source.organization: National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS)
source.page_title: Gout: Diagnosis, Treatment, and Steps to Take

general_guidance.text: Nutrition and lifestyle changes can accompany gout care, but the source notes that they may not be sufficient when gout involves frequent flares or tophi.

foods_emphasized.text: The DASH pattern discussed by NIAMS includes vegetables, fruit, whole grains, low-fat or fat-free dairy products, poultry, and oils.

foods_limited.text: The source identifies alcoholic beverages, sugar-sweetened drinks, red and organ meats, and certain seafood as items to limit or avoid.
Foods and drinks high in saturated fats or added sugars are also limited in the DASH pattern described on the page.

relevant_nutrients.text: Purines are relevant because the source identifies some purine-rich foods in its gout diet discussion.

source.organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI)

general_guidance.text: The source presents iron-rich foods and vitamin C as general dietary context while noting that iron deficiency can also result from blood loss or problems absorbing iron.
general_guidance.source_section: How do you prevent iron-deficiency anemia?

foods_emphasized.text: Food sources listed by NHLBI include beans, dried fruit, eggs, lean red meat, salmon, iron-fortified breads and cereals, peas, tofu, and dark green leafy vegetables.
foods_emphasized.source_section: How do you prevent iron-deficiency anemia?

foods_emphasized.text: Vitamin C-rich foods such as oranges, strawberries, and tomatoes are identified as helping the body absorb iron.
foods_emphasized.source_section: How do you prevent iron-deficiency anemia?

relevant_nutrients.text: Iron is needed to make healthy red blood cells, and vitamin C can help the body absorb iron from food.
relevant_nutrients.source_section: What causes iron-deficiency anemia?; How do you prevent iron-deficiency anemia?
